Logic: (1st number + 2nd number) × 11 = 3rd number.

questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
A + B means ‘A is the son of B’,
A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’,
A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and
A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’.
Based on the above, how is P related to R if ‘P × S ÷ M − T + R’?
questions.solution: Thus, P is R's grandson or son’s son.

questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 ÷ 4 + 8 × 8 − 4 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are
interchanged?
16 ÷ 4 + 8 × 8 − 4 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 16 ÷ 4 + 8 × 8 − 4 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged:

⇒ 16 × 4 − 8 ÷ 8 + 4 = ? ⇒ 16 × 4 − 1 + 4 = ? ⇒ 64 − 1 + 4 = ?

⇒ 68 - 1 = 67.

questions.question: Which of the following operations should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 12 + 12 − 4 × 4 ÷ 2 = 22
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following operations should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
12 + 12 − 4 × 4 ÷ 2 = 22
questions.solution:
Option  2): ÷ and −

12 + 12 − 4 × 4 ÷ 2 = 22 ⇒ 12 + 12 ÷ 4 × 4 - 2 = 22

⇒ 12 + 12 ÷ 4 × 4 - 2 = 22 ⇒ 12 + 3 × 4 - 2 = 22 ⇒ 12 + 12 - 2 = 22 ⇒ 24 - 2 = 22 ⇒ 22 = 22 (LHS = RHS)

questions.question: Six letters J, K, L, M, N and O are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figure below. Find the letter on the face opposite to J.
questions.questionHtml: Six letters J, K, L, M, N and O are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figure below. Find the letter on the face opposite to J.
questions.solution:
As O is common on both the dices, it is clear that M, N, K, and J are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. L will be opposite to it.

​

Opposite pairs:

N → J, M → K, O → L

So, the opposite side of "J" will be side "N".

questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cards are postcards. Some postcards are books. All books are novels. Conclusions: I. Some postcards are novels. II. No card is a book. III. All cards are novels.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
All cards are postcards.
Some postcards are books.
All books are novels.

Conclusions:
I. Some postcards are novels.
II. No card is a book.
III. All cards are novels.

options.text: Only II and III conclusion follow
options.html: Only II and III conclusion follow

options.text: Only I and II conclusion follow
options.html: Only I and II conclusion follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some postcards are novels → Follow (As some postcards are books and all books are novels. As some part of the postcards is common with books which whole comes in novels, therefore it is false.)

II. No card is a book → Does not follow (As all cards are postcards and some postcards are books. As no direct relation is given between cards and books, therefore it is false.)

III. All cards are novels → Does not follow (As all cards are postcards, some postcards are books and all books are novels. So it is possible but not definite.)

questions.question: Each vowel in the word 'STAMINA' is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the third from the right and the fourth from the left in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.questionHtml: Each vowel in the word 'STAMINA' is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the third from the right and the fourth from the left in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.solution:
Given word S T A M I N A

Vowel → (-1)

Consonant → (+1)

 (+1) (+1) (-1) (+1) (-1) (+1) (-1)
Resultant T U Z N H O Z

Now, the number of letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the  third from the right and the fourth from the left in the group of letters thus formed:

(Left end) T U Z N H O Z (Right end)

Here, five letters i.e. I, J, K, L, and M are between H and N.
